title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 133
paragraphs: Having taken command of the force, Miltiades sailed against Paros, under the pretext that the Parians had first attacked Athens by sending triremes to Marathon along with the Persians — this was the excuse he put forward publicly, but he also had a private grudge against the Parians on account of Lysagoras son of Tisias, a Parian by birth, who had denounced him to Hydarnes the Persian. So when Miltiades arrived at his destination, he laid siege to the Parians with his army, first shutting them up within their walls; and sending a herald in to them he demanded one hundred talents, saying that if they refused to pay, his army would not withdraw until it had conquered them completely. The Parians had no intention of giving Miltiades any money; they thought only of how they might defend their city, and among many other contrivances they adopted this one: wherever at any point the wall was exposed to attack, they raised it to double its height under cover of night.
